Why Medford Homes Face Unique Gutter Challenges

Medford sits inside the pine-and-oak forest belt that defines this part of New Jersey. Pitch pine needles, cedar sap, oak catkins, and fine pine grit drop steadily from spring through late winter, and standard slotted screens simply strain them into the trough instead of shedding them.

Once those needles pack in, water back-pitches behind the fascia and the aluminum trough starts to corrode from the inside — a specific failure mode we see on almost every un-guarded roof in Medford, NJ. Summer thunderstorms and the freeze-thaw pattern common to Burlington County then wedge that mat of debris in place until it lifts the drip edge.

The fix is not a bigger screen — it is a 316 stainless steel micro-mesh installed on a rigid, powder-coated aluminum frame. LeafBlaster Pro gutter guards keep every pine needle, catkin, and oak tassel on the roof surface where wind can sweep it off, and the marine-grade mesh does not rot, rust, or sag under wet debris.

Pine-needle proof

Surgical-grade 316 stainless micro-mesh (50-micron aperture) is finer than a pitch-pine needle, so nothing bypasses the guard into the Medford trough.

Resin & sap resistant

Cedar sap and pine resin bead off the stainless mesh instead of gluing debris to the guard, keeping flow rates constant year after year.

Frame that does not rot

Powder-coated aluminum sub-frame carries the mesh above the trough, so packed pine debris cannot back up against the fascia in Medford, NJ.

Why do standard gutter screens fail against Medford's tree canopy?

In Medford, NJ, that is exactly why we install LeafBlaster Pro 316 stainless micro-mesh instead of a slotted screen or foam insert.

Burlington County sees repeated freeze-thaw cycles from December through March.
